description: Compute the next three occurrences, each with start and end, that a schedule would produce, without saving anything. Use it to check a recurring schedule before create_maintenance_window or update_maintenance_window; for a saved window's occurrences use get_maintenance_window. Requires a key with the write scope. An invalid schedule is a 422 with the reason. Returns an array. Example: {"dtstart": "2026-10-18T03:00:00", "duration_minutes": 60, "rrule": "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU", "timezone": "Europe/Berlin"}

dtstart.description: The first start, an ISO 8601 date-time in the wall-clock time of timezone, for example 2026-10-14T22:00:00. A UTC offset or Z is a 422.

duration_minutes.description: How long each occurrence lasts, 1 to 40320 minutes.

rrule.description: Repeats the window: one iCal RRULE without the RRULE: prefix, at most 1024 characters, for example FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU;BYHOUR=3. Hourly, minutely and secondly frequencies are refused. Omit it for a one-time window.

timezone.description: IANA zone name such as Europe/Berlin, at most 64 characters. The schedule repeats in it, so a weekly 03:00 stays 03:00 across daylight-saving changes. Defaults to the organization's timezone.

name: preview_maintenance_window
title: Preview a maintenance schedule
